⺌.etymology: The compressed top form of 小 xiǎo “small”; similar-looking forms in some characters have other origins.
⺌.uncle_hanzi: remnant from 小 in 肖 | 龸 remnant from 尚尙

⺍.etymology: A 小-like component shape; sometimes related to 小 xiǎo “small,” but often created by simplifying unrelated older components, as in 學→学 and 覺→觉.

⺗.etymology: A bottom component form of 心 xīn, originally a pictograph of the heart → emotions, thought and intention.

⺮.etymology: The top form of 竹 zhú “bamboo,” originally depicting two bamboo branches with hanging leaves.

默.etymology: Originally a quiet dog 犬 quǎn that does not bark, with 黑 hēi “black” supplying the sound → silent, quiet.
默.uncle_decomp: Compound 默 | from black-ink 黑𪐗 hēi and | dog 犬 quǎn.

鼓.etymology: 鼓 gǔ “drum; beat” — 壴 zhù depicts a drum on a stand, while 支 zhī “branch; support” originally depicts a hand holding a stick: a hand beating a drum → drum, beat, rouse.
鼓.uncle_decomp: Compound 鼓 alternate 鼔 | from drum 壴 zhù and | hand-grabbing-branch 支𠦙𣏃 zhī | C201 鼓<皷> simp 鼓.

鼻.etymology: 鼻 bí “nose” — 自 zì “self” was originally a pictograph of a nose; after 自 came to mean “self,” 畀 bì “give” was added as a phonetic to preserve the original meaning “nose.”

齐.etymology: Traditional 齊 pictured grain heads lined up evenly → even, uniform, equal; simplified to 齐.

齿.etymology: 齿 chǐ “tooth” — originally a picture of teeth inside a mouth; 止 zhǐ “stop” was added as a phonetic component (possibly confused with 之 zhī “go”), and traditional 齒 simplified the mouth and teeth to 凵 kǎn “container” + 人 rén “person,” which are only graphical shapes here.

龄.uncle_hanzi: the age of a child or adult is told by his teeth).
龄.uncle_decomp: Compound 齡 | from teeth (齿)齒歯 chǐ and | phonetic give-orders 令 lìng | simp 龄.

龙.etymology: 龙 · lóng · dragon — simplified form of 龍, an ancient pictograph of a dragon; 龙 itself derives from a cursive abbreviation of 龍.
龙.uncle_hanzi: animal snake with inverted 王 on its head | cursive left side 丿 remnant 匕
